summary: IDS feed s177_triple is degraded: 3 faults detected - duplicates (8.4%), TCP packet drops (9.3%) and tool overload (1.44 Gbps bursts vs 1 Gbps port). Overload is driving drops and blinding IDS stream reassembly.

findings.root_cause: 8.4% duplicates (209/2483) indicates overlapping capture points - same traffic mirrored from multiple SPANs/TAPs or both directions of an aggregated link fed to the broker without deduplication. Classic triple-feed aggregation without dedup window.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes cycles processing same packet twice, inflates flow counts, bloats state tables and risks false-positive correlations and missed true positives due to duplicate-induced noise.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication (5-10ms window) to suppress duplicates before IDS, preserving IDS capacity for unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: 9.3% TCP gaps (217/2332 packets with missing sequence) indicates buffer exhaustion and drops at SPAN/mirror source or broker egress. Strongly correlated with 1.44 Gbps bursts exceeding IDS port - SPAN cannot handle microbursts and drops randomly.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot reassemble TCP streams or reconstruct full payloads it requires; signatures fail, file extraction breaks, and exploits in dropped segments are completely missed.

recommended_fix.why: Passive TAP has no buffer/drop behavior like SPAN. Replacing SPAN with TAP and aggregating via packet broker eliminates mirror drops and provides lossless feed, essential for IDS full-payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Peak 1.44 Gbps in 1ms bursts vs 1 Gbps IDS port (144% capacity, 6 overloaded intervals). Aggregate feed rate exceeds tool port speed - undersized IDS port for triple-aggregated feed.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC discards excess traffic randomly under burst, causing additional uncontrolled packet loss beyond SPAN drops; detection coverage collapses during bursts when attacks are most likely to hide.

recommended_fix.why: Load-balance 5-tuple hashed flows across 2+ IDS members or upgrade to 10G tool port to absorb 1.44 Gbps bursts without loss while preserving both directions per flow for IDS state.
